objective: Separate the two candidate explanations for the periodic hill's finest rung refusing to converge, by testing the cheap numerical one before the interesting physical one: retighten under-relaxation on the same mesh first, and only if that fails, run the same mesh unsteady and look for a Strouhal number in the residual plateau
rationale: The 2026-08-05 in-house periodic hill ladder produced an anomaly nobody had registered a prediction for. Three rungs at 7,728, 15,600 and 31,280 cells agree on a reattachment length of 7.6436, 7.6472 and 7.6546 hill heights, a spread of 1.4 percent over a fourfold cell range, and two of the three print the solver's own convergence sentence. The fourth rung at 62,400 cells, built by the same generator, passing the same mesh gates at max non-orthogonality 39.80 and max skewness 0.118, does not converge and its residuals do not fall: sampled every 500 iterations the initial residual on Ux sits at 1.17e-2, 1.27e-2, 1.73e-2, 1.07e-2, 7.3e-3, 6.5e-3, 8.1e-3, 1.06e-2 and on pressure at 0.214 through 0.297, a limit cycle four thousand iterations wide and three to four decades above where the coarser rungs stood at the same count. Two readings fit and the results record refuses to choose between them without evidence. The physically interesting one is that at this resolution the separated shear layer stops admitting a steady solution, which would make sense of a case whose reference data are time-averaged LES of a genuinely unsteady flow, and would mean every steady RANS periodic hill result in the literature exists only because its discretization was diffusive enough to suppress the unsteadiness. The dull one is that the relaxation factors of 0.5 on velocity and pressure and 0.7 on the turbulence quantities are the benchmark case's own, tuned at the shipped resolution, and a mesh four times finer simply needs tighter ones. Prediction, written before the run: the dull explanation will NOT account for it, because a relaxation-limited SIMPLE solve usually diverges or crawls rather than sitting on a flat plateau for four thousand iterations, but it is one cheap run and the order matters, because declaring an unsteadiness finding that a relaxation factor would have removed is the kind of claim this lab has had to retract before.
gate: Run one: the same 62,400-cell mesh with velocity and pressure relaxation dropped to 0.3 and the turbulence quantities to 0.5, same 6,000-iteration cap. PASS for the dull explanation if the solver prints its own convergence sentence or the initial residuals fall by three decades; if it does, the anomaly is numerical, the reattachment number from that mesh joins the ladder, and no unsteadiness claim is made. Run two, only if run one fails: the same mesh under an unsteady solver, long enough for at least ten shedding periods at the shear-layer frequency, with the verdict being whether the force or a probe signal carries a resolvable dominant frequency. A plateau with no dominant frequency is a third answer and is reported as one rather than forced into either box
cost_basis: measured for run one and estimated for run two. Run one is the identical mesh and iteration cap as the rung that produced the anomaly, whose cost is recorded in this campaign's own results file, so it prices at that rung's measured core-minutes. Run two is an unsteady solve on the same 62,400 cells and is estimated, not measured; the lab's one relevant measurement is that a pitching-airfoil case on a mesh smaller than its steady sibling ran 15 to 25 times longer in wall time at a Courant-limited time step, so an unsteady periodic hill could overrun this figure substantially and the item should report a partial result rather than spend past it
expected_knowledge_gain: Either answer changes what the lab may claim about steady RANS on separated flows. If it is numerical, the ladder gains a fourth rung and the reattachment number is confirmed grid-insensitive over an eightfold cell range instead of a fourfold one. If it is unsteadiness, the finding is that the steady periodic hill solution is an artifact of insufficient resolution, which bears directly on the closure challenge because the periodic hill is its training-case class and every correction fitted to a steady baseline inherits the assumption that a steady baseline exists
citations: The F6b ERCOFTAC results record of 2026-08-05, section 4, which states both readings and refuses to choose
The F6b ERCOFTAC pre-registration of 2026-08-05, whose gates this anomaly does not disturb

Frohlich, Mellen, Rodi, Temmerman and Leschziner, Highly resolved large-eddy simulation of separated flow in a channel with streamwise periodic constrictions, Journal of Fluid Mechanics 526, 19 to 66, 2005
launch_prompt: F6b periodic hill, the finest rung will not converge. Read demo-output/website/campaign/F6b_ERCOFTAC_RESULTS.md section 4 first, then the pre-registration. DO RUN ONE FIRST AND DO NOT SKIP IT even though the interesting answer is run two. Run one: copy demo-output/website/campaign/F6b_runs/veryfine, drop relaxationFactors to p 0.3, U 0.3, k 0.5, omega 0.5, keep endTime 6000 and residualControl 1e-6, solve serially with setsid and poll the log inline. If it converges, the anomaly is numerical: add the rung to the ladder in F6b_runs/gate.py, report the four-rung grid sensitivity, and make NO unsteadiness claim. Only if run one fails: run two, pimpleFoam on the same mesh with a Courant-limited timestep, long enough for ten shear-layer periods, with a probe in the shear layer and the bottom-wall force written every step; report the dominant frequency and its Strouhal number on hill height and bulk velocity, or report that there is no dominant frequency, which is a third answer and must not be forced into either box. Budget 55 core-min total, 2 cores, and report a partial result rather than spending past it -- run two is an estimate and unsteady cases have overrun this lab by 15 to 25 times before. Pre-register the prediction for each run before launching it. Record: evidence file in demo-output/website/campaign/, docket update on this item, honest verdict.
